chapters.title: Sonny's path into integration and why enterprise integration gets complex
Logic Apps, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, consumption vs. standard
The connector ecosystem and its security trade-offs
Authentication, managed identities and least privilege
Observability, tracked properties and business-driven logging
Organism as a Service: agent loops and self-healing integrations

takeaways: Azure Integration Services combine Logic Apps, API Management, Azure Functions, Service Bus and Event Grid, and the right mix depends on whether a team prefers low code or pro code.
Secure integrations rely on built-in connectors where possible, managed identities, Key Vault and least-privilege permissions so that one breached connection cannot take down every integration.

With agent loops in Logic Apps, integrations can interpret errors and intent and react to unexpected situations, turning integration as a service into what Sonny Gillissen calls Organism as a Service.
hook: Enterprise integration is usually invisible until it breaks, and deterministic workflows struggle with the unexpected. This episode is for architects and integration developers who want to understand Azure Logic Apps, connectors, identity and observability, and how agent loops can make integrations adaptive and self-healing.
